learningObjectives: Use Rescan to update an existing Module when the SUT's UI changes.
Apply Value Range to restrict acceptable values for a Control.
Perform Module Merge to combine two Modules into one and resolve duplicate scanning.

elements.description: Re-scans an existing Module's Controls against the live SUT to update their technical properties — without deleting or recreating the Module.

elements.title: When to use Rescan:
items: A UI redesign changed an element's class, ID, or attribute
A developer updated an element's property that Tosca uses to identify it
A new, more reliable property became available for identification
After a SUT deployment that modifies UI elements

elements.text: Do NOT delete and recreate a Module when the SUT changes — this breaks all TestCase references. Rescan UPDATES the existing Module in place, preserving all references.

elements.title: How to rescan (Exercise 18 procedure):
items: Open the SUT page you want to rescan and leave it open.
Right-click the Module → choose to rescan it.
Keep the already-selected Controls AND add any new Controls (e.g., 'Update shopping cart' button, 'Apply coupon' button).
Rename Controls during the rescan for business readability (e.g., 'discountcouponcode textbox' → 'Enter discount code').
Use 'Mark on Screen' to locate the correct element (e.g., to identify the right table).

elements.text: Rescan is like updating your contact book when a friend moves — you don't create a new contact, you update the existing address so all references to that contact remain valid.

bulletPoints: Rescan = update in place. All TestCases referencing the module automatically use the updated properties.
During a rescan you can ADD new Controls and RENAME existing ones — not just refresh properties.
Use Rescan proactively after any SUT deployment that changes UI elements.

elements.description: A property set on a Control within a Module that defines the list of acceptable values for that Control. Acts as a validation layer at the Module level.

elements.title: How Value Range works:
items: Defined on the Control inside the Module — not on the TestCase or TestStep
Restricts what values can be entered or verified for that element
If a TestStep tries to use a value outside the range, Tosca flags it as invalid
Common use case: a dropdown that only accepts 'EUR', 'USD', or 'GBP'

elements.description: When entering multiple values into a Value Range, separate them with semicolons and use NO spaces between values.
items: Correct: AutomationDiscount2;PercentageTotal;PercentageShipping;FlatTotal
Wrong: AutomationDiscount2, PercentageTotal (commas + spaces)
Wrong: AutomationDiscount2; PercentageTotal (spaces after semicolons)
Separator = semicolon ( ; ) only. Spaces would be treated as part of the value.

elements.text: Value Range is defined at the Module/Control level — it applies everywhere that Control is used, across all TestCases.

bulletPoints: Value Range prevents invalid test data errors at the source — the Module definition.
More robust than per-TestCase validation: define once, enforced everywhere.
Separate range values with semicolons and NO spaces: value1;value2;value3.

elements.description: Combines two separate Modules that represent the same SUT element into one authoritative Module. After merging, all TestSteps referencing either original module are updated automatically.

elements.term: Target Module vs. Source Module (key exam concept)
elements.description: In a merge, one Module is the Target and the other is the Source.
items: Target Module = the one you KEEP. It survives the merge.
Source Module = the one that gets DELETED after its selected Attributes are copied into the Target.
If the wrong Module is set as Target, use the 'Switch Modules' option to swap them.
You choose which Attributes to bring from the Source into the Target.
Tosca automatically links Attributes that have identical properties in both Modules.

elements.title: How to merge two Modules (Exercise 18 procedure):
items: Select both Modules simultaneously using CTRL+Click.
On the Modules tab in the top ribbon, select 'Merge Modules'.
Confirm the correct Module is the Target — if not, click 'Switch Modules'.
Select the Attributes to bring from the Source into the Target.
Tosca 15.0+: if a Self-Healing steering parameter warning appears, click the red cross icon to remove that property.
Click 'Merge' — Tosca reports how many Attributes were updated, relinks all usages, and deletes the Source Module.
Click 'Close' and rename the surviving Module if needed.

elements.title: Why merge duplicate Modules:
items: Duplicate Modules are created when multiple team members scan the same SUT page independently
Maintaining two Modules for the same element doubles the maintenance effort
A SUT change would need to be applied to both duplicates — merge eliminates this risk
After merge: one authoritative Module, all TestCase references consolidated

rows: Two Modules exist for the same SUT element

elements.text: Module Merge is like deduplicating your contact list: if 'John Smith' is entered twice with slightly different phone numbers, you merge them into one complete, authoritative entry.

bulletPoints: Module Merge: same SUT element scanned twice → merge into one.

examPitfalls.title: Rescan ≠ delete and recreate
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Distractors suggest deleting the old Module and creating a new one when the SUT changes. This would break all referencing TestCases.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Rescan UPDATES the existing Module in place. All TestCases continue to reference it without changes.

examPitfalls.title: Value Range is set on the Module, not the TestCase
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates place Value Range configuration in the TestStep or TestCase properties.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Value Range is a property of a Control inside a Module. It constrains what values are permissible for that Control everywhere it is used.

examPitfalls.title: Module Merge purpose
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask when to use Module Merge. Candidates confuse it with Rescan (updating an outdated module).
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Module Merge = combining duplicate Modules into one. Rescan = updating a single Module's properties from the live SUT.

examPitfalls.title: Value Range separator — semicolon, no spaces
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates separate Value Range entries with commas or add spaces after the semicolon. Spaces become part of the value and break matching.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Separate Value Range entries with semicolons and NO spaces: value1;value2;value3. Commas and spaces are wrong.

examPitfalls.title: Target Module survives, Source Module is deleted
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates think the Source Module is kept, or that both survive. In a merge, the Source is deleted after its Attributes are copied to the Target.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Target Module = the one you keep. Source Module = the one deleted. If the wrong one is set as Target, use 'Switch Modules' before merging.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After a SUT deployment, a button's HTML class attribute changed from 'btn-primary' to 'btn-action'. The existing Module still references the old class. What is the correct action?

options.text: Rescan the existing Module to update the Control's properties with the new attribute.
Delete the old Module and scan the button again to create a new one.
Manually edit every TestStep that uses this Module to reflect the new attribute.
No action needed — Tosca automatically detects SUT changes.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Rescan updates the existing Module's Control properties from the live SUT. This is far safer than deleting and recreating (which would break TestCase references) or manually editing every TestStep.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester notices that the same 'Login' page was scanned by two team members, resulting in two separate Modules for the same page with overlapping Controls. What is the recommended solution?

options.text: Keep both Modules and use whichever is more complete.
Use Module Merge to combine the two Modules into one authoritative module.
Delete one Module and manually update all TestCases that referenced it.
Use Rescan on both modules to synchronize their properties.

practiceQuiz.hint: Two Modules for the same element = merge them.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Module Merge combines duplicate Modules into one. After merging, all referencing TestSteps are updated automatically. Keeping both creates maintenance burden; deleting one requires manual TestCase updates.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Currency' dropdown Control should only accept 'EUR', 'USD', or 'GBP'. A tester wants to enforce this constraint at the Module level. Which feature should they use?

options.text: Use ActionMode Constraint to restrict the value.
Add a Verify step in every TestCase that uses this Control.
Create a separate Module for each currency option.
Set a Value Range on the Control in the Module.

practiceQuiz.hint: The constraint belongs at the Module/Control level.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Value Range is a Module-level property that defines acceptable values for a Control. Setting it on the Currency Control ensures that any TestStep using that Control is automatically restricted to the allowed values — no per-TestCase verification needed.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester adds four discount codes to a Value Range on a Control. Which entry is formatted correctly?

options.text: Code1, Code2, Code3, Code4
Code1; Code2; Code3; Code4
Code1;Code2;Code3;Code4
Code1 Code2 Code3 Code4

practiceQuiz.hint: Semicolons, and watch out for spaces.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Value Range entries are separated by semicolons with NO spaces: Code1;Code2;Code3;Code4. Commas (A) are wrong. Spaces after semicolons (B) become part of the value and break matching. Spaces alone (D) are not a valid separator.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During a Module Merge, the tester wants to make sure the correct Module is kept and the duplicate is removed. Which statement is true about the Target and Source Modules?

options.text: The Target Module is kept; the Source Module is deleted after its Attributes are copied over.
The Source Module is kept; the Target Module is deleted.
Both Modules are kept and linked together.
Tosca randomly chooses which Module to keep.

practiceQuiz.rationale: The Target Module is the one you keep; the Source Module is deleted after its selected Attributes are copied into the Target. If the wrong Module is set as Target, use 'Switch Modules' to swap them before merging.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester is rescanning a Module and notices a newly added 'Apply coupon' button on the page that is not yet in the Module. What can they do during the rescan?

options.text: Nothing — rescan only refreshes properties of existing Controls.
Add the new Control to the Module and optionally rename it during the rescan.
They must create a separate new Module for the button and merge it later.
Delete the Module and start a fresh scan to include the button.

practiceQuiz.hint: Rescan can do more than refresh — it can grow the Module.
practiceQuiz.rationale: During a rescan you can keep the already-selected Controls AND add new ones (like the 'Apply coupon' button), and you can rename Controls for readability. You do not need to create a separate Module or delete and recreate the existing one.

quickRecap.value: Updates an existing Module's Control properties from the live SUT. Preserves all TestCase references.
Set on a Control in the Module. Restricts allowable values for that Control across all TestCases.
Separate values with semicolons, NO spaces: value1;value2;value3.
Combines duplicate Modules (same SUT element scanned multiple times) into one authoritative module.
Target = kept. Source = deleted after Attributes copied over. Use 'Switch Modules' to swap. CTRL+Click both → Modules ribbon → Merge Modules.
Right-click Module → rescan. Can refresh properties, ADD new Controls, and RENAME Controls — all without breaking references.
